_note: 6E Standard (400) powersets. AUTHORED — there is no legacy 6E prose to lift, unlike the 5E sets.
Two things aim these, and neither is a point total:
1. The powers BUDGET is whatever the archetype's characteristics leave of the 400, minus the
50-point skills bucket. It is computed, never declared — see allocate/characteristicsBudget.
Brick 121 · Patriot 148 · Martial Artist 153 · Speedster 164 · Energy Projector 185
Powered Armor 190 · Metamorph 191 · Weapons Master 191 · Mentalist 204 · Mystic 208
Gadgeteer 228
2. The RULE OF X (core/random/ruleOfX, ported from Phil's Rule of X.xlsx) is what says whether
the finished character is balanced. Spending the budget exactly proves nothing — two
archetypes can both spend 400 and be wildly apart. The 400pt campaign baseline is:
EGO 13 · CON 20 · DEX 24 · SPD 5 · CSL 2 · OCV 8 · DCV 8 · OMCV 3 · DMCV 4
DC 12 · oAP 60 · DEF 26 · rDEF 17 · STUN 40 · BODY 10 · dAP 30 · Velocity 40
...and the band is ±10%. SPD and DC/oAP carry weight 20 each — the heaviest — so an
archetype that runs hot on either has to give the points back somewhere.
The characteristics are already fixed by archetypes.6e.json, so a powerset's job is the rest:
DEF/rDEF (via Resistant Protection), oAP/DC (the attack), dAP, and Velocity.
Shape (same as the 5E sets): a framework container lives under its own key with its reserve in
`basecost`, and its slots are siblings in `power` linked by `parentid`. The key IS the framework
type — normalizeCharacterData stamps originalType from it.
6E notes: ARMOR is gone (Resistant Protection, still xmlid FORCEFIELD, does both jobs), Force
Wall is Barrier, and Flight is 1 point per metre — so Velocity 40 costs 40.

Energy Projector.label: Energy Blaster
Energy Projector._note: starborne is the corpus model: a 12d6 blast (oAP 60, DC 12 — dead on the baseline), Resistant Protection carrying the defences, and Flight for the velocity. The last 18 go on flavour starborne itself carries (Flash Defense, Nightvision, Life Support) — it spends the budget and the Rule of X barely sees it, which is the point: not every power is a combat stat.
